name: Haiku concentrated AI/technology
strategy: Supply-chain-anchored AI infrastructure thesis emphasizing ASML (EUV bottleneck for chip production) and enterprise software adoption (MSFT, CRM) with reduced cloud infrastructure and semiconductor concentration, positioned for structural AI capex tailwinds with defensive stops.
reassessment_note: Round 3 book underperforming SPY (+2.64% vs +3.26%) despite 85% invested. Current market headwinds: Oracle force majeure on data center construction; Treasury yields rising; NVDA facing insider selling ($2.2B/12mo) despite operational excellence. Structural opportunity: ASML is sole EUV supplier with 60+ shipments planned for 2026 (+25% YoY), less cyclical than discrete semiconductor bets. Shift capital from SNOW (infrastructure delay vulnerability) into ASML (true bottleneck). Maintain enterprise AI exposure (MSFT Copilot relaunch, CRM Agentforce adoption). Trim NVDA due to cyclical valuation concerns and insider activity. Add QCOM custom silicon exposure. Stops remain as guardrails for macro deterioration.

positions.thesis: ASML is the sole producer of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines—an irreplaceable bottleneck in AI chip supply chain. Targeting 60+ EUV shipments in 2026 (+25% YoY) driven by memory fab adoption and AI data center buildout. Less cyclical than discrete semiconductor producers; geopolitical moat from export restrictions strengthens competitive position. Structural capex leverage as hyperscalers scale training infrastructure.

Enterprise AI adoption accelerating: Microsoft relaunched Copilot product signaling shift of value creation from infrastructure vendors to commercial AI application layer. Azure cloud services benefiting from sustained capex spending. +1.52% since entry (2026-09-21) despite broader sentiment volatility; largest institutional support among mega-caps for enterprise AI.

Custom silicon opportunity with leading hyperscaler underway; initial shipments expected in Q4 2026. Diversifies beyond PC/server/gaming. Competitive with NVDA on AI accelerator roadmap but valued lower due to execution risk. Supply chain tailwind from ASML EUV capacity expansion. 60% YTD performance reflects market belief in category growth.

Salesforce Agentforce enterprise AI agents are capturing commercial AI adoption wave. Recurring subscription model insulates from infrastructure capex volatility. Operating leverage as platform scales. Shift from infrastructure capex to enterprise software adoption is structural trend; CRM positioned as core enabler. -3.87% from entry vulnerable to macro, but 50% TP reflects enterprise AI tailwind.

Qualcomm entering custom silicon space with leading hyperscaler; initial December Q shipments add non-cyclical revenue stream not tied to smartphone unit cycles. Up 13.6% on 2026-09-28 on this announcement. Smaller position captures upside while limiting downside to smartphone demand cycles. Strategic shift away from handset dependency.

Core exposure to AI accelerator market, but trimmed from 8% due to valuation concerns (41.8% 'undervalued' yet marked as possible value trap by GuruFocus). Insider selling of $2.2B over 12 months and only 12 of 33 tracked gurus increasing positions signal caution. $150B buyback is positive but reflects limited growth optionality at current valuation. Maintains stake in AI infrastructure while reducing cyclical risk.

Data platform benefiting from AI infrastructure buildup, but Oracle's force majeure on Project Jupiter (New Mexico data center) and Morgan Stanley/Jefferies reports of construction delays create near-term headwind. Cut from 16% to 8% to reduce infrastructure capex cycle exposure. Maintain smaller position for tactical data platform upside if delays resolve. -3.32% from entry within stop zone suggests market has already repriced.
